title: Your map app relies on Einstein
summary: Clocks on GPS satellites run about 38 microseconds a day fast because of relativity. Without correcting for it, positions would drift by around 10 km per day.

scenes.text: Your phone's map relies on Einstein.
GPS satellites carry atomic clocks. Your phone works out where it is from how long their signals take to arrive.
Relativity pushes those clocks in two directions.

left.label: Weaker gravity
left.text: Clocks high up tick faster: about +45 μs a day

right.label: High speed
right.text: Moving clocks tick slower: about −7 μs a day

scenes.text: Net result: satellite clocks gain about 38 microseconds every day.
Tiny? Radio signals travel about 300 metres in one microsecond.
scenes.reveal: Left uncorrected, positions would drift by roughly 10 km per day.

scenes.text: So the satellite clocks are deliberately set to tick slightly slow before launch.
